main_text.p: Sensus interior est tum concipiens, tum confer-vans.
Concipiens est sensus internus, rerum sensibilium à sensibus externis oblatarum imagines suscipiens.
Sensus communis est, qui sensibilia à sensibus exterioribus oblata, sive communia, sive propria, definit & discernit.
Communia sensibilia sunt adjuncta rerum communia, propter quę species sensibiles à sensibus exterioribus apprehenduntur; quęq; propter sensum communem à pluribus exterioribus sensib. percipi possunt.
Talia sunt: magnitudo & figura corporum, à visu & tastu; item motus & quies corporum, atq; numerus, ab omnibus exterioribus sensibus communiter etiam sensibilia.
Organon sensus communis est in anteriore parte cerebri, geminis ventriculis constante, sensuum exteriorum organis proximâ.
Hic propterea sensus in somno unà cum sensibus externis prorsus cessat & quiescit.
Solo interiore isto sensu prædita animalia, sunt Pisces; item vespertiliones, mures, glires, mustelæ, cæteraq; his cognata.
Phantasia est sensus internus, species à Sensu

page.notes: Long s is plain s throughout. Lines "Estq;" and "Solo interiore" are read from the scan; the word "constante" is followed by a comma as printed. Ligatures and italic words were transcribed as shown. Page ends mid-sentence, continuing on the next page. Words "Communia sensibilia" heading italic at start of paragraph is kept as printed. "Phantasia" at page end is italic as printed. The page-end line "Phantasia est sensus internus" is set in the same type as the text; "Sensu" is the last word on the page. Note: the printed text reads "cerebri" with a partly obscured "c"; read as "cerebri". Some ink is faint in the middle of the page (around "corporum" and "quies"), but these words were legible.
